kids: 🛡 Starlane: your weapons switch off near space stations so you can’t hit one by accident
📦 Nova tells you when your hold is too full to pick up a canister
🚀 Launching and docking now go properly through the hangar door, and your ship’s name sits on the hull
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader: weapons safe near stations (Pause → Controls → Flight assists, on by default, all devices) — within 10 km of a station lasers and missiles are held, and they arm again at once if you are attacked. Tours and the guided flight are not affected.

📦 Full cargo hold: when a canister appears and there is no room, Nova and the screen say so; flying into it no longer smashes it or damages the ship, and the radar card explains why it cannot be scooped.

🎬 Launch and docking cut scenes: the ship now flies through the middle of the hangar opening (it used to pass through the wall below it), and the cameras stay inside the hangar and look out through the opening.
🎨 Your ship’s name is painted onto the hull surface on both sides instead of floating beside it.

kids: 🧲 The tractor beam in the Black-Hole Time-Warp works with every FIRE button
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader: the tractor beam in “The Black-Hole Time-Warp” now responds to every FIRE control — keyboard, mouse, gamepad and both touch FIRE buttons (it ignored the side FIRE button on tablets and folds). While you are grabbing or towing the meteor, FIRE works the beam only, so your lasers no longer shoot the meteor you are trying to catch.

kids: 🌌 Adventures in Starlane now have your full attention — no pirates or other chatter interrupting the story
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader: adventures are exclusive — random arrivals pause, other ships nearby leave when a space adventure starts, and only the adventure’s own lines are spoken, so the narration and its words stay in step.
📱 On touch screens the on-screen FIRE and joystick are hidden while a puzzle panel is showing (the game is paused until you answer), so it no longer looks as though FIRE has stopped working.

kids: 🚀 Starlane now sits inside a spaceship wall with portholes, instead of plain black edges
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader: wherever the game picture does not fill the screen (docked screens, menus, in-ship adventures, Retro flight, phones), the surround is now a ship’s bulkhead with ribbed panels, strip lights and portholes instead of plain black.

📱 Adventure puzzles use slightly larger text on small screens; every scene of all 50 adventures was checked at phone size. One over-long answer in “The Rusty Robot” was shortened. The 1969 capsule now floats closer so it can be seen.

kids: 🌫️ The nebula is now real fog all around your ship, and hyperspace fills the whole screen
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader: fixed the nebula appearing as a rectangle on wide screens — in the Modern style it is now real 3D fog (stars hidden, distant objects fade, cockpit stays clear) and all adventure effects (fog, solar storm, planets, suns) are drawn across the whole wide view. Hyperspace now fills the full screen in the Modern style when there is room at the sides.

🧪 Test mode stages adventures where they would really happen: hyperspace adventures make a real jump first; the rest start cruising in open space (after-battle ones with wreckage ahead). Test scenarios start in open space. Leaving test mode returns you to exactly where you were.
🛸 Faction ships no longer arrive during the guided first flight.

kids: 🛸 Five new kinds of ship to meet in Starlane: the Halo Seeker, Scrapjaw raiders, the giant Verdant Ark, the super-fast Quicksilver and the crystal Thorn Bloom
🌌 Space adventures now happen out in space — real nebula fog, a solar storm you can see, and an alien ship that flashes its lights at you
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader — five original faction ships with their own 3D looks (Halo Seeker, Scrapjaw, Verdant Ark with Seed fighters, Quicksilver, Thorn Bloom). They visit systems from time to time; Scrapjaw packs raid lawless systems; the radar card shows each faction. Test mode has a “Meet the faction ships” scenario.

🌌 Space adventures are staged in the world: puzzles appear in a compact panel over the live view; the ship turns to open space; Lost in the Nebula has real fog and scanner interference; Solar Storm shows the growing corona, particle streams, cabin heat and an aurora in the planet’s shadow; First Contact has the Lathari ship flashing real light patterns; The Sleeping Ship is a Verdant Ark; Mars, Eclipse, Aurora, Goldilocks, Star Shell, Twin Suns, Gas Dive, Galaxy Edge, Capsule 1969, Moon Base and Ice Moon each show their own scene.

kids: 🛟 Starlane flight assists — easier flying on tablets: a joystick that appears under your thumb, a ship that stays level, help with aiming and docking
🗺️ Much better-looking maps, with planets, mission icons and a card for each system
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader flight assists (Pause → Controls → FLIGHT ASSISTS), with separate settings for touch screens (on by default) and mouse & keyboard (off by default): floating joystick with fine control near the middle (touch), auto-level, aim assist, auto-fire (off by default everywhere), turn to target (tap a radar icon, the 🎯 button or key 7), docking assist (lines up the slot and matches the spin — you control speed) and pop-up DOCK / JUMP / E.C.M. buttons (touch).

🗺️ Maps: space backdrop with spiral arms, stars coloured by economy, government or tech on every map, visited systems solid, mission and hazard icons, glowing fuel range and route, animated target, rendered planets on the short-range chart, a grid and slow rotation on the 3D map, and a system card with a planet picture, details, fuel and trading tips.
🛒 Shipyard: category tabs evenly spaced, description under the list, one fuel button.

kids: 📱 Starlane is bigger on tablets and folds held sideways — the game now fills the full height of the screen
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader on touch screens in landscape full screen: the game uses the whole screen height (about a third more picture on a tablet); the score strip and Pause / Exit / Stop shrink into the top corners; in the Modern style the 3D space view fills the side margins behind the touch controls. Laptops and big screens with a mouse are unchanged.

kids: 📱 Starlane works properly on tablets and phones: the joystick steers, FIRE lets go when you lift your finger, and in full screen there are big controls at the sides
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader on touch screens: fixed the on-screen joystick (it never steered) and FIRE (it never switched off) — both were mistaken for subtitle dragging. In full-screen landscape on tablets and folds, the game now shows a joystick on the left and FIRE, BOOST, MISSILE and a speed slider on the right, outside the picture; each lets go reliably even if the touch is cancelled. Laptops and big screens with a mouse are unchanged.
👪 Grown-ups on iPads, tablets and phones: triple-tap the score strip at the top of a game (or the app title on the home page) instead of Ctrl+Shift+G.

kids: 🎨 Starlane adventures look much better — real-looking planets and moons, and detailed pictures
🖥️ The adventure task now shows on your ship’s MISSION screen
items: 🚀 Starlane Trader: adventure pictures redrawn — planets, moons, Mars, gas giants, the Sun and asteroids are now rendered globes with lighting and atmospheres; space scenes have starfields and nebulae, ship scenes a lit metal cabin, and everything sits in a display frame. During an adventure’s flying task, the goal, timer and target distance appear on the MISSION screen (the right console wing in widescreen, or the small mission screen) — tap it to flip between ADVENTURE and MISSION. Without those screens, the panel sits top-left and ⇄ moves it above the console.
